feedback: Approved as a baseline. Iteration 0 has no earlier race data, so this review rests only on the contract and the candidate's own contents. Nothing here states how the candidate will perform. The geometry is valid: five sensors at 15 mm spacing, a 12 mm footprint on a 25 mm tape, and sensor x running from +0.03 (left) to -0.03 (right) with weights [2, 1, 0, -1, -2], so the sign convention matches the contract. All values sit inside their ranges. Only one review run remains this iteration and no revision round fits in it, so a revise decision would leave the iteration unscored. Race it now and use its telemetry to sharpen the next iteration. Read the results this way: if completion is 0, or completion_time is near or above 3 s, raise base_speed (for example to about 1.8) before changing steering. If steering_oscillation is high, or rms_error is large while the robot still completes, lower kp or raise kd (for example kd about 0.3). If line_loss_events are frequent on the s-bend or slalom, keep last_direction and reduce base_speed on the tighter bends. If the robot leaves the track (progress below 1 with completion 0 and max_error near 0.06), widen the body_width or lower base_speed.
requested_changes: After the baseline race: if completion_time is at or above about 2.8 s or completion is 0, raise base_speed to about 1.8 and leave the steering gains unchanged for one comparison.
If steering_oscillation is high while rms_error is above about 0.02, lower kp toward 1.5 or raise kd toward 0.3, with sensor_weights unchanged.

If line_loss_events is above 0 on the s-bend or slalom, keep line_loss as last_direction and reduce base_speed by about 0.2 on those tracks' tighter sections, or consider widening sensor_positions spacing only if losses persist.
